Title: Recursive source walk and diff
Detail: Walks SourcePath recursively writing one manifest row per file (SR-001); Compare-SourceToBackup returns the pure NewOrChanged/RemovedFromSource diff consumed by the run.

Title: xxHash128 file hashing
Detail: Streams the file through System.IO.Hashing.XxHash128 and formats big-endian bytes as 32-char uppercase hex (SR-002); Initialize-XxHashLibrary guarantees the type is loaded.

Title: Content-addressed dedup keying
Detail: Groups source rows by (xxH2Hash,Length) and copies the physical data once per key (SR-003); Get-HashSizeFileName derives the content-addressed name; later names flagged Duplicate.

Title: Extension-gated 7-Zip storage
Detail: Test-ShouldCompress decides by extension only (SR-004); Compress-FileWithSevenZip writes a .7z whose extension is appended to the stored name so Compressed and filename agree. WP5 merged the eight extensions the HomeHub deployer's list carried (.jar .tgz .zst .gif .webm .ogg .sav .pack) into $script:NonCompressibleExtensions, which remains the ONE definition site; Office/text formats are deliberately excluded because SN-003's acceptance line says a .docx/.txt IS stored as .7z. README's 'Already-compressed extensions' table is checked against the live list by TC-096 so the documentation cannot drift. Compress-FileWithSevenZip removes an existing destination BEFORE the '7z a', because 'a' ADDS to an archive rather than replacing it: the write path is index-authoritative, so an UNREFERENCED object at the content-addressed name (a run killed before its manifest was written, a row evicted while its object awaits prune, interrupted-7-Zip debris) would otherwise be merged into (WP9 review nit-4, taken 2026-08-26).

Title: Dated snapshot completion
Detail: Builds the snapshot in Temp staging then, when the manifest state changed (Compare-SourceToBackup diff non-empty — NOT the physical-copy counter, which misses dedup-served adds and shared-content removals), renames it to Snapshot_<prior-backup-date> after its manifest is written (SR-005); no snapshot for a manifest-identical run or the latest/live state; same-second disambiguator preserved. An optional -BackupTime seam (cf. Test-HashRecalcDue -Now) dates the snapshot deterministically for tests.

Title: Refcount-aware eviction
Detail: Evicts a removed file's data to staging only when no surviving manifest row references its (hash,size) (SR-006); shared data is retained (B9).

Title: Restore-kit deposition
Detail: Copies Reconstruct.ps1, reconstruct.sh, FileBackup.Common.psm1, System.IO.Hashing.dll, RECONSTRUCT.paths.json and RECONSTRUCT.bat into the live backup and each dated snapshot (SR-007). Common imports nothing from Engine (load-bearing split).

Title: Standalone reconstruction
Detail: Rebuilds the tree from the manifest using bundled Common (SR-008); decompresses .7z rows via Expand-FileWithSevenZip and recovers blank-DataPath rows by scanning for a content-hash match.

Title: Restore target guard
Detail: Rejects a restore target located inside the backup folder before writing any file, and refuses any manifest row whose canonicalized destination falls outside the target root — the row is warned, counted unrestored, and fails the run per SR-029 (SR-009).

Title: Point-in-time restore authority
Detail: When launched from a Snapshot_<date> folder, uses that snapshot's own manifest as the sole authority (no newer-manifest overlay) and resolves bytes by (xxH2Hash,Length) via Find-DataFileByHash over the data pool = backup root + all snapshot folders (SR-010). The scan's infrastructure-name skip is root-level only per SR-022 (a nested infra-named file is data and a legitimate recovery source, B6); matching is by (hash,length) — the skip is an optimization, not a correctness gate.

Title: Rehash scheduling decision
Detail: Test-HashRecalcDue maps A/E/D/W/M/Y/N + last-run + injectable -Now to a recalc boolean (SR-011); Get/Set-LastHashRun persist the timestamp in FileBackupState.json.

Title: Per-set isolation and exit code
Detail: FileBackup.ps1 loops Invoke-BackupSet per set updating an OverallSuccess [ref] (SR-014); a set's failure is logged without aborting the loop and yields exit 1.

Title: Conditional non-fatal mail
Detail: Sends mail only when SMTP fields are present and -NoMail is unset (SR-015); Send-MailMessage failure is caught and logged WARN, never changing exit status (B15).

Title: Non-interactive automation path
Detail: -NonInteractive threads from FileBackup.ps1 through Initialize-Dependencies into Resolve-OptionalTool (degrade missing tool to absent) and Initialize-XxHashLibrary (-AutoInstall or throw with guidance) so an unattended run never blocks on a prompt (SR-016). AMENDED 2026-08-24 (kit-bump rev6): Reconstruct.ps1 gains a [switch]$NonInteractive, documented in the param() block comments alongside -ExitCode and -RequireWitness. When -TargetRoot is omitted, -NonInteractive (or [System.Console]::IsInputRedirected as defense-in-depth) prints usage via a new Show-ReconstructUsage helper - text mirroring reconstruct.sh's usage parameter-for-parameter - and exits 2 (usage/precondition), matching reconstruct.sh's existing required --target-root; the interactive Read-Host prompt is kept, unchanged, for hand use. RECONSTRUCT.bat passes %* so no bat change is needed.

Title: Stale staging abort
Detail: Detects a pre-existing Temp staging folder under ChangePath and aborts with a message naming it (SR-017) rather than overwriting a half-written prior run.

Title: Missing-config guard
Detail: Tests ConfigPath with -PathType Leaf and throws "Config file not found" before any work (SR-018).

Title: External-tool resolution
Detail: Resolve-OptionalTool/Initialize-Dependencies locate configured tools; missing 7-Zip fails before any compression-enabled set is processed, while missing ffprobe leaves MediaMBPerSec blank (SR-020).

Title: Literal/bracket-safe paths
Detail: All file ops use -LiteralPath and [System.IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName/GetFileName instead of Split-Path -LiteralPath -Parent/-Leaf (which throws on PS7), keeping Unicode/bracketed names intact (SR-021).

Title: Root-only infrastructure test
Detail: Classifies kit/manifest names as infrastructure only at the backup root (SR-022); nested same-named user files are data (B6). The allowlist covers every artifact New-ReconstructScript deploys, including the RECONSTRUCT.paths.json sidecar (2026-07-02 review).

Title: Restore capacity check
Detail: Sums required bytes using decompressed sizes for .7z rows and compares against target free space before restoring (SR-023, B10/B11). The target volume is now measured by Get-FreeSpaceBytes (Common, SR-052) instead of Get-PSDrive over Split-Path -Qualifier, which errored on a rooted POSIX path and was swallowed by the adjacent catch, leaving this check silently inert on Linux and in the container. An unmeasurable volume still SKIPS the check rather than refusing.

Title: Deterministic manifest output
Detail: Stable row ordering + typed serialization make an unchanged re-run produce byte-identical manifest rows (SR-024).

Title: Manifest schema round-trip
Detail: Read/Write-Manifest are the only IO for the 9-column schema, preserving typed Length/LastWriteTime, tolerating null/empty, and returning @() for a missing file (SR-025).

Title: Cross-change duplicate collapse
Detail: After a run, collapses identical data shared across change folders to a single stored copy still resolvable from each (SR-026).

Title: Dated-snapshot storage and clean cutover
Detail: Persists each set's last backup-completion time in FileBackupState.json (new Get/Set-LastBackupRun) to date the next snapshot; snapshots keep the full pre-run manifest plus only superseded bytes (Move-RemovedFilesToStaging) deduped by Optimize-ChangeFolders; the ^Snapshot_ regex replaces ChangeFolderRegex in Get-FileBackupDefaults and engine/Reconstruct drop all Pre_*_Changes handling (SR-028). Set-LastBackupRun accepts an injectable -When for deterministic test timelines.

Title: Config builder and quick-start
Detail: CredSetEx.ps1 plus the README quick-start let a new user produce a valid CLIXML config and run a first backup (SR-027); System.IO.Hashing auto-installs on first use.

Title: Reconstruct unrestored-row accounting
Detail: The restore loop records every row it skips (blank-DataPath hash-recovery failure, missing DataPath, extraction failure) instead of silently continuing; after the loop a non-empty list logs an INCOMPLETE summary and throws, so a scripted pwsh -File caller exits non-zero (SR-029). A clean run keeps exit 0.

Title: Bash xxh128 wrapper
Detail: hash_file wraps xxhsum -H128 / xxh128sum, normalizing output to the 32-char uppercase big-endian hex Get-FileXxHash emits (SR-030). Lives inside the single self-contained reconstruct.sh (no sourced runtime libs, per plan pinned decision); the bottom-of-file main guard lets bats source the script to unit-test the function. Conformance pinned by golden fixtures under tests/fixtures/hash-conformance/.

Title: Bash standalone restorer
Detail: reconstruct.sh restores from the backup root or a Snapshot_<date> folder with the SR-031 semantics, mirroring Reconstruct.ps1: authority selection by the script's own folder name (^Snapshot_ regex), RFC-4180 manifest parse, RelativePath backslash-to-slash mapping, data-pool (backup root + all snapshots) hash recovery for blank/missing DataPath rows, 7z expansion of compressed rows, target-inside-backup guard, capacity pre-check, and unrestored-row accounting with a non-zero exit naming the count (mirrors SR-029). Single self-contained file; tool preflight fails loudly with remediation (SN-015 pattern).

Title: Manifest portability layer
Detail: parse_manifest does RFC-4180 CSV parsing via gawk FPAT (handles quoted fields with commas/embedded quotes) and tolerates a UTF-8 BOM; to_posix_path maps RelativePath backslashes to '/'; LastWriteTimeStr is treated as opaque ISO-8601 'O' text (never reparsed/reformatted). Both are functions inside the self-contained reconstruct.sh, unit-tested by sourcing it under bats (SR-032).

Title: Bash backup engine
Detail: Produces contract-conformant backups (manifest schema, dedup, short names via the shared alphabet, .7z gating, dated snapshots, refcount eviction) interoperable with the PowerShell engine (SR-033). Phase bash-v2 — decompose further before implementation.

Title: Container lifecycle workflow
Detail: Builds a digest-pinned non-root image, checksum-verifies the baked System.IO.Hashing package, runs a compressed backup from a read-only source using a separate writable source-state mount and byte-exact restore smoke test, exports docker-loadable tar archives, and tags/pushes/pulls fully-qualified OCI image references without accepting registry secrets as arguments.

Title: Run-state integrity gate
Detail: Invoke-BackupSet reads the prior backup date before any mutation and throws when it is null while the existing MANIFEST.csv still has rows, and an unparseable FileBackupState.json surfaces as a failure rather than an empty first-run state — so a non-initial run can never take the first-backup branch of Complete-ChangeFolder that discards staged history (SR-035).

Title: Empty-source refusal
Detail: When Update-SourceManifest returns zero rows for a source whose backup MANIFEST.csv still has rows, Invoke-BackupSet removes its staging folder and throws unless Set.AllowEmptySource is true; the error names the surviving row count and the override key (SR-036).

Title: Portable tool resolution
Detail: SevenZipDefaultPath is seeded from $env:FILEBACKUP_7ZIP_PATH (no module-scope Windows path construction); Initialize-Dependencies prefers the set's Tools.SevenZipPath, and the missing-7-Zip remediation names both knobs (SR-037).

Title: Witness sidecar writer
Detail: Write-Manifest writes MANIFEST.csv then calls Write-ManifestWitness, which computes Get-FileXxHash over the written file, emits Version/Rows/Bytes/XxH128/Written as UTF-8 (no BOM) LF key=value lines to MANIFEST.csv.meta.tmp in the same folder and publishes it with Move-Item -Force (atomic rename over any prior sidecar). Both helpers live in Common because Reconstruct.ps1 may call only Common (AGENTS.md sec.3, guarded by TC-048). WitnessFilename is added to Get-FileBackupDefaults and to Test-IsInfrastructureFile's root-level allowlist beside RECONSTRUCT.paths.json, together with MANIFEST.csv.meta.tmp — a crash between the WriteAllText and the Move-Item leaves that staging file behind, and a leftover must not be backed up as user data nor warned about as an orphan. Rows is supplied by Write-Manifest (it already holds the records it wrote) instead of re-reading the manifest with Import-Csv; a standalone re-stamp omits it and the file is counted. Snapshots inherit their own witness because Complete-ChangeFolder rewrites the staging manifest through Write-Manifest before the rename; the sidecar is deliberately NOT added to the kit-artifact copy list (that would overwrite the snapshot's witness with the backup root's) (SR-038).

Title: Restore-side witness verification
Detail: Test-ManifestWitness (Common) parses MANIFEST.csv.meta, compares Bytes/Rows/XxH128 against the manifest on disk and returns a verdict object (Verified|Absent|Mismatch|Malformed) plus the failing field and an optional non-fatal Warning. Fields are checked Bytes -> Rows -> XxH128, but a Rows-only disagreement defers to the digest: bytes and digest matching means the manifest IS the witnessed one, so it verifies with a warning (counting-semantics divergence) rather than aborting; with no digest present the row count still aborts. Reconstruct.ps1 calls it inside Read-RawManifest's replacement, after the manifest-exists check and BEFORE the target folder, the RECONSTRUCT.log and the capacity pre-check are created, so an exit-2/exit-3 refusal writes nothing at all into the target (its log lines are buffered and flushed once the log exists); it adds the CSV header-shape check that bash already performs; bash/reconstruct.sh gains verify_manifest_witness (grep/cut key=value, wc via parse_manifest, xxh128sum) at the same point in main(), immediately after the existing header guard. Absent sidecar = WARN and continue unless -RequireWitness/--require-witness (SR-039).

Title: Restore exit-code taxonomy
Detail: Find-DataFileByHash returns [pscustomobject]@{Path;Cause;Detail} with Cause in Found|ContentMissing|DependencyMissing|StorageUnreadable|CandidateError (search folders are probed for existence/readability, an archive candidate met without a usable 7-Zip yields DependencyMissing, a caught extraction error yields CandidateError); the restore loop records {RelativePath;Cause;Detail} per unrestored row and the summary classifies them into the content class (exit 1) and the host class (exit 4). Exit-Reconstruct centralizes logging plus, under -ExitCode (passed by RECONSTRUCT.bat), 'exit <code>'; otherwise it throws, preserving the existing message wording so in-process callers and the harness keep working. A script-level trap routes any terminating error the script did NOT classify to the precondition class (exit 2 under -ExitCode, rethrow otherwise) so an unexpected failure can never be reported as data loss (1); the target-folder and log creation route their own failures through the same class, matching reconstruct.sh's 'mkdir -p || die' (2) for a file occupying the target path. reconstruct.sh keeps die()=2 and gains die_code() for 3 and the 1-vs-4 split at the end of main(); its usage text and header comment carry the table (SR-040). AMENDED 2026-08-24 (kit-bump rev6, SR-040/SR-056): the locator's return set is reduced to Found|DependencyMissing|StorageUnreadable|ContentMissing - CandidateError is never returned by Find-DataFileByHash/find_by_hash, because it would be dead code once ContentMissing is the fallback; a candidate that fails to expand is data damage (folded into the ContentMissing detail, ' ; N candidate(s) could not be expanded: <first>'), while a candidate that cannot be read at all is the host condition StorageUnreadable. The restore LOOP's own CandidateError (the row's own file failed to expand/copy) is unchanged and stays host-class. A candidate that cannot be read records exactly one cause, never CandidateError plus DependencyMissing (the no-7z double record, fixed at the same site). bash/reconstruct.sh currently has no read-error arm distinguishing StorageUnreadable from a failed expand - left as a known asymmetry pending the Windows-host implementation. Amended 2026-08-24 (review): Test-SevenZipUsable / sevenzip_usable self-test gates the damage classification of expand failures; WriteMismatch added to the host-cause set. Amended 2026-08-25 (Terra review): bash gained the candidate read-error arm (hash_file failure => StorageUnreadable, single record - PS parity), and BOTH restorers surface an unlistable snapshot tree as StorageUnreadable/exit 4 instead of silently shrinking the recovery pool.

Title: Move-loop failure aggregation
Detail: Both move loops take [ref]$OverallSuccess (as Invoke-BackupFileGroup already does), wrap the Move-Item plus its destination-directory creation in try/catch, and on failure log 'Failed to <evict|preserve> ...: <message>' at ERROR, add the entry to a local failure list, set OverallSuccess to false and continue; each returns/logs a summary count so a partially staged snapshot is explicit. Invoke-BackupSet passes the ref and proceeds to Complete-ChangeFolder so staging is never orphaned (SR-017) (SR-041).

Title: Validating configuration loader
Detail: Import-BackupConfiguration (exported from Engine, not Common — config loading is backup-only and Common must stay restore-safe) dispatches on the file extension, replacing FileBackup.ps1:100-125. The JSON branch parses with ConvertFrom-Json, requires an integer ConfigVersion within [1,$script:ConfigSchemaVersion], runs Assert-NoUnknownConfigKey over the top level, Tools, Secrets and each set (rejecting Secrets.Credential explicitly), then Test-BackupConfigurationShape; the CLIXML branch runs Test-BackupConfigurationShape only, preserving today's message wording so existing expectations hold. Type checks read the parsed JSON node's actual type — a quoted "false" is rejected rather than passed to [bool], which would coerce it true. Resolve-BackupSetDefaults materializes SourceStatePath=SourcePath and AllowEmptySource=$false and upper-cases HashRecalcFreq, so the engine's [bool] and ToUpperInvariant casts become belt-and-braces. Errors are terminating, single, first-in-document-order, and name the JSON path. container/FileBackup.schema.json is the published draft-07 mirror (additionalProperties:false) used for documentation and TC-077, not at runtime — keeping it out of the image and off the Dockerfile COPY list (SR-042). Test-BackupConfigurationShape -StrictTypes type-checks every schema-defined value through Test-ConfigValueJsonType (string/boolean/integer/object/array; 'integer' accepts any integral-valued JSON number, culture-safely and without [math]::Floor, whose BigInteger overload is ambiguous for a number beyond Int64), and names the offending set by its real array index rather than a literal [?]. ConfigVersion is range-checked before the [int] cast, so an out-of-range version is refused as unsupported rather than by fractional-representation luck. tests/Common/ConfigFixtures.ps1 is the single fixture corpus consumed by TC-074, TC-075 and TC-077, so the published schema (whose BackupSets anyOf and ConfigVersion const now match the validator) cannot drift from it; TC-077 calls Test-Json with -Json/-Schema strings because the -Path/-SchemaFile forms need pwsh 7.4, above this repo's PowerShell 7+ floor.

Title: Entry-point status codes
Detail: FileBackup.ps1 gains [switch]$ExitCode and wraps the Import-BackupConfiguration call: on failure it writes the message to stderr and, when the switch is set, to the global log path before 'exit 2'; without the switch it rethrows so & $entry keeps throwing for tests/Unit/Engine.Tests.ps1 and the harness. The trailing 'if (-not $overallSuccess) { exit 1 }' is unchanged, so Coverage.Tests' exit-1 expectation (TC-034) holds in both modes. container/entrypoint.sh adds -ExitCode to the exec argument list ahead of "$@". The code meanings match WP1's restore table (0 complete / 1 incomplete / 2 usage-precondition) so one vocabulary covers both halves of IF-001 (SR-043). Exit-ConfigFailure also covers the missing/unreadable config file: the Test-Path existence check routes through it instead of a bare throw, so a missing file exits 2 under -ExitCode. Logger creation is deferred until AFTER Import-BackupConfiguration succeeds (New-Logger truncates via New-Item -Force, so building it earlier destroyed the previous run's log on a config typo); config-time messages such as the multi-set WARN are buffered and flushed once the log exists, and Exit-ConfigFailure writes to stderr plus an APPEND to the global log only when that file already exists, creating nothing.

Title: Container distribution roundtrip + incremental snapshot smoke
Detail: Adds an Action=Load verb (docker load wrapper, mirrors Export) to Invoke-Container.ps1; CI's container job chains BuildAndTest -> Export/Load roundtrip -> Publish/Pull roundtrip against a throwaway registry:2 service, re-running -Action Test after each reload. Invoke-ContainerSmokeTest gains the RECONSTRUCT.paths.json artifact check and a second incremental run (source mutated between two docker run invocations) that asserts a Snapshot_<date> folder appears, then restores both the latest state and the snapshot alone in separate restore containers, byte-comparing each against the correct source generation.

Title: Prune plan and re-homed copy
Detail: Get-SnapshotPrunePlan builds the pool index through Get-BackupContentIndex, derives the demand set (every row outside the target with a blank DataPath, or a non-blank DataPath whose file is absent -- Test-BackupManifest can blank root DataPaths in a damaged store), and emits one plan item {Key, SourceFullPath, SourceDataPath, SourceRow, DestinationFolder, DestinationDataPath, DestinationRow, Compressed, StoredAsHashSize, Bytes} per endangered key. Destination election mirrors Optimize-ChangeFolders: the backup root when it demands the key, else the newest demanding snapshot by FolderOrder. The destination name IS the source row's DataPath: under content addressing a data file's name derives from its content and stored form, so a re-homed object's destination name is always identical to its source name (the S3 collapse, measured at WP9 step 8 and taken 2026-08-26 when legacy path-addressed support was withdrawn; the 30-line Get-ReHomedDataPathName synthesizer and its legacy arm are deleted). A name that would classify as root-level infrastructure at the destination, or that would overwrite a DIFFERENT file already there, is recorded as a Code=2 problem instead of an item; an identical file already there is treated as an interrupted prune's completed copy (resume). Copy-ReHomedDataFile copies with -LiteralPath to '<destination>.fbprune.tmp', verifies stored-form identity (length plus Get-FileXxHash equal to the source) and, unless -SkipContentVerify, content identity against the row's xxH2Hash/Length -- expanding a '.7z' to a temp file first, exactly Find-DataFileByHash's check -- then publishes with Move-Item -Force. Publish-PruneManifest mutates only DataPath/Compressed/StoredAsHashSize on the destination row held in the plan's Manifests table and persists through Write-Manifest, never Export-Csv and never a direct Write-ManifestWitness call, so the SR-038 witness is re-stamped by its one writer and MANIFEST.csv.meta is never copied between folders.

Title: Prune rails, pool proof and commit point
Detail: Assert-PrunePrecondition RETURNS the full set of {Code,Kind,Message} refusals rather than throwing on the first (a documented deviation from the work order's 'throw' wording: Remove-BackupSnapshot applies the 2 > 3 > 4 > 1 precedence over the whole set, and -WhatIf can report every refusal at once). It checks: the target is an existing ^Snapshot_ folder that is a direct child of the resolved change root and carries no wildcard (2); the SR-035 run-state gate via Read-BackupState -- a malformed state file, or a populated backup manifest with no LastBackupRun (2); no Temp staging folder in the change root (2, SR-017 mutual exclusion); the plan's own Code=2 problems (unknown target, infrastructure name, destination collision); unreferenced data files in the target, from Get-DataFile against the target's own manifest, unless -DiscardUnreferencedData (2); Test-PoolResolves over the WHOLE pool, so an already-broken pool or a pre-existing form disagreement refuses rather than being pruned into (2); free space on each destination volume for the planned bytes via Get-PruneCapacityRefusal, which groups items by Get-VolumeIdentity and probes Get-FreeSpaceBytes (Common, SR-052) and SKIPS an unmeasurable volume rather than refusing (2) -- WP4 grouped by Split-Path -Qualifier inside a Group-Object key, which cannot parse a UNC or rooted POSIX path and left the rail non-existent on a UNC store; 7-Zip present when the plan carries a compressed row and content verification is on (2); and Test-ManifestWitness on EVERY pool manifest -- Mismatch/Malformed (3), Absent (3) unless -AllowUnverifiedIndex. Test-PoolResolves rebuilds the index over the pool minus an excluded folder and reports every row that would not resolve, plus form disagreement: Compressed='Yes' with a located file that is not '.7z', or Compressed='No' with a '.7z' located file whose row's RelativePath is not itself '.7z' (which would be a legitimately stored already-compressed source file). Complete-PruneDeletion renames the folder to 'Pruning_<name>' -- the commit point, since that name fails $Def.ChangeFolderRegex and both restorers' ^Snapshot_ patterns -- then Remove-Item -Recurse -Force. Residue handling is split in two (WP4 review, H1/H2/M1). Remove-CommittedPruneResidue runs BEFORE the named snapshot is planned, deletes only 'Pruning_<that same name>' (past the commit point, invisible to every consumer, and it holds the name the plan needs), and is wrapped so a host failure is a code-4 record instead of an unclassified throw; it is skipped entirely under -WhatIf. Invoke-PruneEntrySweep now runs INSIDE the transaction, after the rails pass and the Temp lock is held, so refusals mutate nothing and its failures land in the code-4 catch; it scans only pool folders (backup root + Snapshot_*) and deletes a '*.fbprune.tmp' only when that folder's OWN manifest does not reference it -- a staged copy is unreferenced by construction, whereas a Mirror-mode user file called 'notes.fbprune.tmp' has a row naming it and is content. The Temp lock is created with New-Item and NO -Force (creation is the atomic test, closing the TOCTOU window between the staging-busy rail and the lock; an already-existing folder becomes the staging-busy refusal, code 2, and the finally block then never deletes a lock this invocation did not create) with its PRUNE.inprogress marker written inside the try.

Title: Shared content index and snapshot inventory
Detail: Get-BackupContentIndex is the literal lift of Optimize-ChangeFolders' inline map: '<xxH2Hash>|<Length>' -> location records {LocationType, Folder, DataPath, FullPath, IsBackup, FolderOrder}, backup root at FolderOrder -1 then the given snapshot folders 1..n in the order supplied (name order, oldest first), skipping blank DataPaths, blank hashes and rows whose file is not on disk -- the index describes bytes that EXIST, so a blank row is demand and never supply. It also returns one Folders record per indexed folder {Folder, Name, Order, Manifest, IsBackup} so a caller reads each manifest once. Optimize-ChangeFolders now consumes it and derives its change-manifest list from the same pass, with no behavior change (TC-089 pins the post-conditions and was run green before the lift). Get-PoolSnapshotFolder filters the change root by the single $Def.ChangeFolderRegex every consumer uses, sorted by name; Get-SnapshotDate parses the point-in-time date out of the folder name, tolerating Complete-ChangeFolder's _NNN collision disambiguator. Get-BackupSnapshot joins the index with each snapshot's manifest and takes PhysicalBytes/BytesReclaimed/BytesReHomed straight from Get-SnapshotPrunePlan, so the reported reclaim is the achieved reclaim by construction. Locations are read out of the index with .ToArray(), not @(...): a List reached through a PSObject property throws 'Argument types do not match' on PS 7.5 (AGENTS.md 4).

Title: Retention at the entry point and the container boundary
Detail: FileBackup.ps1 gains [ValidateSet('Backup','Prune','Snapshots')]$Action='Backup' and [string[]]$Snapshot. Prune and Snapshots resolve the single configured set through Import-BackupConfiguration + Resolve-BackupSetPaths and dispatch to Remove-BackupSnapshot (with -WhatIf passed through and -SevenZipPath from the resolved dependencies) or Get-BackupSnapshot piped to ConvertTo-Json; under -ExitCode the SR-040 code from the batch result becomes the process exit code, otherwise a non-zero outcome throws for in-process callers. The Backup path is untouched, so every existing invocation behaves exactly as before. container/entrypoint.sh reads FILEBACKUP_ACTION or shifts a leading positional word in {backup,prune,snapshots}; anything starting with '-' is left in "$@" and flows through unchanged (TC-060/TC-076 unaffected), FILEBACKUP_SNAPSHOT becomes -Snapshot and a truthy FILEBACKUP_DRY_RUN becomes -WhatIf. bash/reconstruct.sh is NOT modified and a source guard pins that it carries no removal path.

Title: Storage-form audit and repair
Detail: Get-StoredFileForm classifies one file as Archive or Raw from its first six bytes (7z magic 37 7A BC AF 27 1C) plus its extension, with no hashing. Test-BackupStorageForm walks the pool through WP4's Get-BackupContentIndex (LLR-047) - backup root at FolderOrder -1 then Snapshot_* in name order - and emits one finding record {Folder, RelativePath, DataPath, Class, Observed, Expected, Repairable} per disagreement; classes NameLies, FlagOverRaw, FlagOverArchive, DanglingDataPath, BlankRowFormDisagreement, Unreferenced. The already-compressed-SOURCE exemption is keyed on the PAYLOAD, not on the file name (WP5 re-review residual HIGH): when the observed form is Archive while the row says Compressed=No, the file's OWN bytes are hashed against the row's (xxH2Hash,Length) - a match is correct raw storage of archive-shaped content and yields NO finding, only a mismatch is a genuine FlagOverArchive - because an already-compressed source can be named anything (archive.7z.bak, a .pack file, an installer payload). A .7z RelativePath stays as the cheap fast path. The confirming hash runs only for that rare shape, so the default (non-Deep) scan stays a six-byte read per row. -Deep additionally verifies payload identity (raw: length+Get-FileXxHash vs the row; archive: the file's own bytes FIRST, since for an already-compressed source stored raw those bytes ARE the payload, and only otherwise expand to temp and hash) and requires 7-Zip. Repair-BackupStorageForm acts only on findings whose evidence is a file in the row's own folder, rewrites Compressed and renames the data file so name and form agree, never re-packs, never touches the six logical columns, and persists each folder with Write-Manifest (never Export-Csv, never a direct Write-ManifestWitness call). Findings are grouped by (Folder, DataPath) - not iterated per row - so the physical rename happens ONCE and every row referencing the old path adopts the observed form, including a row exempted from the flag rewrite by the payload-keyed already-compressed-source rule, whose bytes' identity is read BEFORE the rename moves them (it follows the file, keeping its own Compressed); repairing per row renamed the file for the first row and then saw Missing for the second, leaving it dangling. Blank-row findings are reported only. Enumeration uses Get-DataFile/Test-IsInfrastructureFile at each folder's own root (root-level only, B6/SN-018). Outcome mapped to the SR-040 table; no call site inside Invoke-BackupSet. The entry point resolves the set's roots with Resolve-BackupSetPaths -ReadOnly inside its try, so verification creates no directory, does not require SourcePath, and reports a missing backup root as code 2.

Title: Hash recovery reports the located file's form
Detail: Find-DataFileByHash's Found result gains a Form field (Archive when the match was proven by expanding a .7z candidate at Reconstruct.ps1:225-238, Raw when proven by hashing the file itself at :243-249); find_by_hash's tuple becomes Found\037<form>\037<path>. The restore loop's hash-recovery branch (Reconstruct.ps1:522-533 / reconstruct.sh:550-575) records the form and the decompress decision at Reconstruct.ps1:548 / reconstruct.sh:583 consults it; the non-blank DataPath branch keeps using the row's Compressed. Every .7z candidate that does not yield the payload is re-tested as raw bytes (length + hash) before it is dropped - whether the expand FAILED (a .7z name over raw content) or SUCCEEDED with other content (a genuine .7z source file stored raw, whose own bytes are the row's content); a CandidateError is recorded afterwards only for the failed-expand case. No new tool, state or manifest column; kit-bundled files change, so both restorers carry # KitRevision: 3. AMENDED 2026-08-24 (kit-bump rev6, SR-040/SR-056): the no-7-Zip double-record nit is fixed at the same raw-bytes-test site - when the raw-bytes test throws, the read failure is recorded once as StorageUnreadable and the candidate loop continues; 7-Zip could not have helped read a file that cannot be read. Only a candidate whose raw bytes were read successfully and did not match still records DependencyMissing. Mirrored in reconstruct.sh's no-7z arm.

Title: Reference-counted deletion at every pool-removal site
Detail: The two steps that remove bytes from the pool both ask the same question before removing anything: does any row of the FINAL manifest still claim this DataPath? Move-RemovedFilesToStaging has always counted references this way (B9); Save-SupersededData was retargeted at WP9 step 4 from a SOURCE-based approximation - which could not see a frozen row (SR-055/SR-057) or a row whose replacement copy failed, and moved out bytes those rows still claimed (D-1's family) - to the same final-manifest claim test. The migration site this LLR originally guarded (Sync-BackupStorageLayout) was deleted whole at WP9 step 3 (SR-061), so the invariant now lives entirely at these two sites.

Title: Cross-platform free-space preflight
Detail: Get-FreeSpaceBytes (Common, so the restore kit stays self-contained) resolves a path's containing volume with System.IO.DriveInfo over the resolved full path and falls back to Get-PSDrive on a drive-qualified path, returning $null only when neither can answer - it never throws. Get-VolumeIdentity takes the identity from the MOUNT TABLE: [System.IO.DriveInfo]::GetDrives() enumerates real mounts on both platforms and the longest mount point prefixing the resolved path on a separator boundary is the answer, with DriveInfo::new as the fallback - on Unix that constructor is the identity function and echoed the path it was handed, so /backup and /backup/sub read as different volumes. Reconstruct.ps1:441-455 consumes it in place of Split-Path -Qualifier + Get-PSDrive, so the SR-023 check works for a rooted POSIX path. Assert-BackupCapacity (Engine) sums the run's additions per volume - new (hash,length) groups not already in the backup manifest at uncompressed Length, plus Sync's pending transformation bytes, plus staging bytes only when ChangePath resolves to a different volume than BackupPath - grouping the backup and change demands by Get-VolumeIdentity so demands on ONE volume are summed against that volume's free space (checking them separately passed two demands that each fit and together did not), and throws a classified precondition failure before any mutation. Invoke-BackupSet calls it after the diff (step 8) and before Save-SupersededData (step 11.5), checked at step 9.4, the last point at which nothing has been written; a refusal fails the set (entry-point status 1) with none of this run's content written and no staging folder orphaned (not a claim that the tree is byte-identical - nothing already stored is ever re-formed (SR-061), so there is no migration to size). No new configuration key (SR-042's schema is closed).

Title: Blank rows re-enter the diff; dedup adoption requires a non-blank DataPath
Detail: Compare-SourceToBackup adds a third NewOrChanged arm: metadata-equal but [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($b.DataPath) (pure diff, unit-tested directly). Invoke-BackupFileGroup's $existingBackupWithHash candidate filter additionally requires a non-blank DataPath, so a (hash,length) group containing only blank rows falls through to the copy branch and every logical name (including the healed row) is pointed at the newly written file. Save-SupersededData is unaffected: a heal row has the same content as its blank predecessor, so the same-content guard skips staging.

Title: Verify runs the pool audit; the blank-row form rail is kit-revision-gated
Detail: Invoke-VerifyAction appends Test-PoolResolves' Kind=broken-pool problems (mapped onto the six-field finding shape as Class=PoolUnresolvable) to the form-audit findings inside the same try, so path failures stay code 2 and findings drive code 1. Test-PoolResolves problem objects gain Folder/RelativePath/DataPath fields (additive). Its blank-row branch consults Get-BackupKitRevision per folder (cached): revision >= 2 skips the located-copy form comparison entirely (SR-050 - the kit decides from the file); below 2 the refusal remains and its message names the kit revision and the -Action Verify -RefreshKits remedy. Broken-pool problem objects carry BytesSurvive (checked on DISK against the content index, excluding the missing path itself); Invoke-VerifyAction maps BytesSurvive=true onto the honest Class=PoolDataPathMissing and only a genuinely byte-less row onto PoolUnresolvable (WP7 review R2), and Get-BackupCapacityDemand excludes blank-DataPath rows from its already-held set so heal copies are budgeted (WP7 review R1). The non-blank-DataPath form check is unchanged.

Title: Portable-name guard in the source scan
Detail: Test-PortableRelativePath classifies one relative path per component (separators: both slashes on Windows, / only elsewhere; the separator array is TYPED - an if-expression unrolls [char[]] to object[] and String.Split then never splits, a latent bug found and fixed at WP9 step 8b) and returns $null or a reason string, including the reserved-device-name stem predicate (CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9, any case, with or without extension). Update-SourceManifest takes an optional -UnportableOut list and skips a failing name BEFORE the open/hash attempt, recording {RelativePath, Reason}. Test-PortableRelativePath carries a -TreatAsPosix seam (defaulting to the real platform) so the Windows unit suite asserts the POSIX-only backslash arm. Invoke-BackupSet step 5.1 logs one ERROR per record, marks the set failed, and step 8 filters the skipped names out of RemovedFromSource so an existing row is frozen rather than evicted.

Title: Restore verify-after-write and one-shot pool recovery
Detail: After a successful expand/copy for a manifest row, the restored destination is hashed and (Length, xxH2Hash) compared against the row; on mismatch the destination is deleted, the existing (hash,length) pool recovery (Find-DataFileByHash / find_by_hash) is attempted exactly once as if the row had a blank DataPath, and the result is verified again. A single verify implementation and a single 'restore this row' implementation are called at most twice per row (Restore-OneRow / restore_one), keeping the restore loop readable. No new -ExcludePath parameter or exclusion state is needed: the pool locator hashes every candidate itself, so a wrong-bytes file cannot be returned as a match. A row that still fails to verify after the one recovery attempt is recorded as the content-class cause ContentMismatch and is not added to the host-cause set (SR-040/SR-056). Amended 2026-08-24 (review): locator-proven mismatch => WriteMismatch host-class, no second search; read-back failure => host-class, file kept (bash restore_one rc=22).

Title: Force hidden/dot capture across every enumeration site
Detail: All nine Get-ChildItem call sites gain -Force, each with a one-line why comment: (1) Engine.psm1 Get-DataFile - the source/pool recursive walk, the D-4 headline, also fixes -Recurse skipping hidden directories entirely; (2) Engine.psm1 Update-SourceManifest external-cache branch - same, bypasses Get-DataFile; (3) Engine.psm1 Optimize-ChangeFolders -Directory scan - a hidden Snapshot_* folder was invisible to sanitization; (4) Engine.psm1 Get-PoolSnapshotFolder -Directory scan - the pool silently omitted a hidden snapshot; (5) Engine.psm1 Get-SnapshotPrunePlan PhysicalBytes accounting - hidden files were deleted but not counted, so the reclaim figure lied; (6) Engine.psm1 Invoke-PruneEntrySweep *.fbprune.tmp scan - hidden residue was never swept; (7) Common.psm1 Expand-FileWithSevenZip temp-dir pick - a hidden extracted payload returned $null and threw; (8) Reconstruct.ps1 Find-DataFileByHash pool scan - hash-addressed short names can begin with a dot, making a hidden pool file unrecoverable by hash; (9) Reconstruct.ps1 snapshot-folder enumeration for the search pool - a hidden snapshot folder dropped out of the pool. reparse-point/symlink traversal semantics are unchanged (D-4 non-goal, pinned by comment + test). bash/reconstruct.sh is a zero-line change (find never skipped dot-files); a comment at reconstruct.sh:298 pins that as intent, alongside find running without -L (link-immunity) as intent. A static Pester guard greps Modules/*.psm1, Reconstruct.ps1 and FileBackup.ps1 for Get-ChildItem occurrences lacking -Force and fails naming the file/line, modeled on tests/Unit/Coverage.Tests.ps1 (SR-057).

Title: Content-addressed copy with owner election and intra-run memo
Detail: Always hash-names the stored object; the (hash,length) group elects its owner (shortest RelativePath, ordinal tie-break) whose extension and Test-ShouldCompress answer define the single physical form; the first member writes it and an in-process memo makes every later member adopt it. The PreserveFolderTree parameter and the SR-022 Mirror-name refusal are deleted.

Title: Superseded-data preservation after copy/evict, survival tested against the final manifest
Detail: Runs after the copy and evict steps (nothing is overwritten under content addressing, so it no longer has to run first) and asks whether any row in the FINAL manifest still claims the old row's DataPath - eviction's own B9 claim semantics. Testing by DataPath is conservative in the direction that matters: a claim always keeps its bytes in the pool, and the one asymmetry - a single content stored under TWO hash names, possible only in a pre-WP9 store because the owner's extension is folded into the name - at worst parks the unclaimed twin in the newest snapshot, still inside the restore pool (review 2026-08-25, MIN-5). The exact test replaces the source-based approximation that authorized D-1's in-place overwrite; frozen rows (SR-055/SR-057) and rows whose copy failed keep their claim in the final map, so their objects now correctly stay in the pool. The Mirror-only legacy source-based arm this clause used to describe was deleted with the mode at WP9 step 5; there is now one code path.

Title: Storage-layout migration deleted; sanitize kept; legacy store refused by engine AND both restorers
Detail: Sync-BackupStorageLayout and Get-MigrationCapacityDemand are DELETED whole (~260 lines), together with the step-5.5 migration capacity preflight and the SR-051 refcount apparatus that existed only to make a migration safe. Invoke-BackupSet step 6 calls Test-BackupManifest directly for the sanitize half Sync used to wrap, which also collapses two overlapping orphan scans into the one that SR-064 makes linear. A row carrying StoredAsHashSize='Original' fails the set before mutation with the fresh-BackupPath remedy. Kit revision 7 (human ruling 2026-08-26) withdraws READ support too: both restorers scan the authority manifest before the target exists and refuse with the precondition code (2) when any row carries StoredAsHashSize='Original' (the authoritative marker, matching the engine) or a DataPath containing a path separator (the structural marker, which still catches a store whose column was lost). Nothing is written. The withdrawn claim is the one WP9 review MIN-2 flagged as untested on the bash half.

Title: Manifest-derived browse view generator
Detail: Writes INDEX.tsv plus per-folder INDEX.html pages and a root search page under the resolved view root (default <BackupPath>_View), names entries from the ROW's Compressed column, stamps a SHA-256 of the canonical manifest ROWS into .viewstamp (deliberately not the manifest witness: a manifest-identical run can rewrite the CSV with different quoting), and refuses a view root that is off-volume or overlaps any owned path in either direction, and - the independent second guard - refuses to WIPE a view root holding anything that is not a generated view (WP9 review MAJ-1). Engine-side only: Common never grows view code (AGENTS.md sec.3).

Title: Linear unreferenced-data audit
Detail: Builds one referenced-DataPath hashtable (the pattern already used at Engine.psm1:761/:772) instead of re-piping the manifest per on-disk file, and keys it with New-RelativePathMap so a case-differing Linux pair is not conflated.

Title: Config contract v2: removed-key refusal and view keys
Detail: ConfigSchemaVersion becomes 2; PreserveFolderTree leaves the closed key set and gains a NAMED diagnostic (not the generic unknown-key message) raised for JSON and CLIXML alike; BrowseView and ViewPath join the key set with their vocabulary and placement checks in Test-BackupConfigurationShape / Resolve-BackupSetDefaults.

Title: -Action View dispatch
Detail: Adds View to the -Action ValidateSet and dispatches a forced view rebuild that reports through the SR-040 status table, alongside the pipeline's own step-16 refresh.

Title: Directory sidecar: empty directories and folder attributes
Detail: Get-SourceDirectoryRecord walks the source with -Force and emits {RelativePath, Attributes} for every directory that is EMPTY of files or carries a recorded attribute bit. Emptiness is decided from the ancestor set of the file rows the walk already produced, never by re-enumerating each directory, so the pass stays linear in directories plus file rows (the SR-064 discipline). A directory the walk could not enumerate is NOT emitted -- claiming empty for an unreadable directory would be a lie in the dangerous direction -- and a non-portable directory name (SR-055) is skipped with a warning rather than failing the set a second time. Get-DirectoryAttributeToken masks to Hidden, System, ReadOnly and NotContentIndexed, the only four SetFileAttributes can apply to a directory; Archive/Temporary/Offline are meaningless on one and Compressed/Encrypted/ReparsePoint/the ReFS integrity bits cannot be set through that API at all. Rows sort ordinally so two runs over the same state write byte-identical sidecars. Write-DirectorySidecar writes DIRECTORIES.csv beside the manifest and REMOVES it when there are no rows, so a tree with no empty or attributed directory is byte-identical to a pre-SR-065 store. Invoke-BackupSet writes it at step 12.5, after the manifest, and step 7 copies the PRIOR sidecar into staging so a snapshot keeps its own point in time; the sidecar is deliberately NOT in Complete-ChangeFolder's kit list. Restore-DirectorySidecar and apply_dir_sidecar run LAST, after every file is written and verified: rows are created parents-first and attributes applied deepest-first, path traversal is refused as it is for manifest rows, and reconstruct.sh creates the directories but reports the Windows attributes as inapplicable on POSIX rather than dropping them silently. The sidecar is ADVISORY and unwitnessed: absent, unreadable or malformed, it leaves exactly the pre-SR-065 behaviour and never fails a restore.

Title: Restored files carry their own modification time
Detail: Both restorers apply the row's own LastWriteTimeStr after the SR-056 (hash,length) verification passes -- including after a hash-recovery retry, so a file that was deleted and re-written never keeps a stamp from the failed attempt. Set-RestoredLastWriteTime parses through ConvertFrom-ManifestDateString and calls File::SetLastWriteTime; stamp_mtime uses touch -d on the manifest's ISO-8601 round-trip form and retries with the fractional seconds stripped for leaner userlands. Neither is ever fatal: the bytes are correct and verified by the time it runs, so a blank or unparseable cell warns and the row still counts restored. ReadOnly does not block it (SetFileTime needs FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES, which a read-only file grants). This is what stops a deduplicated row inheriting the pool object's timestamp: the mtime used to ride along on the copy, so every twin got the OWNER's.

Title: Bounded copy retry with a per-run budget
Detail: Invoke-BackupFileGroup's candidate loop is wrapped in ATTEMPT ROUNDS: each round tries every member of the content group, then waits and retries the whole list. Get-CopyRetryDelayMs returns 250 ms then 1000 ms and finally $null, so three attempts cost at most 1.25 s of waiting per file. Test-CopyFailureIsTransient returns false only for the n6 directory-destination refusal, which cannot change by waiting; everything else is treated as possibly transient, because guessing wrong that way costs time while guessing wrong the other way costs the file. The destination is cleared between rounds by the same Remove-Item the MIN-1 fallback uses, so a retry never lands on partial debris (and never merges into it, SR-004). RetryBudgetMs is a [ref] the SET owns - Invoke-BackupSet seeds one per set and passes it to every group - so a systemically unreadable tree cannot sleep the run away; omitting it (a direct unit call) yields a fresh local budget. On exhaustion the error names the attempt count and states the file is NOT in the backup, no row is added to BackupMap, and OverallSuccess goes false. A row from an EARLIER run survives untouched, the same frozen-row treatment SR-055/SR-057 give a file the walk could not read. Covered at BOTH levels: the group-level cases build the group by hand and delete or lock the source, and an end-to-end case deletes a source file inside the real walk-to-copy window using a separate sniper process keyed on the step-5 source hash cache (the parent runspace is blocked on the backup child and cannot pump a FileSystemWatcher, which is why an in-process watcher never enters the window).
